name: DoorLoop
description: DoorLoop is property-management software for property managers, owners, and landlords across residential, multifamily, single-family, commercial, affordable-housing, and community-association portfolios. Teams use it for properties, units, leases, tenants, owners, rent and fee collection, accounting, financial reports, maintenance, listings, applications, eSign, tenant screening, owner portals, resident communications, files, workflows, AI tools, and integrations.
agentUseSummary: DoorLoop cannot yet be connected through Relay as an enabled provider. DoorLoop publishes REST API documentation and partner materials, but official materials say API access is for approved developers and selective partner/customer use; Relay needs an approved credential, exact API terms, scope/resource boundaries, and property-management governance before mounting any tools.

blocked.label: Connect DoorLoop
blocked.description: DoorLoop has an API, but public materials describe approved-developer/selective access. Relay has not been approved for credentials, API terms, resource boundaries, rate limits, tenant binding, revocation, or live acceptance.

blocked.label: Read DoorLoop records
blocked.description: Properties, units, portfolios, leases, tenants, owners, vendors, accounts, charges, payments, deposits, bills, expenses, reports, maintenance, communications, files, listings, applications, screening, and portal records remain unavailable to Relay.

blocked.label: Change DoorLoop records
blocked.description: Creating, updating, importing, posting, paying, charging, reconciling, messaging, screening, signing, assigning, uploading, archiving, deleting, or otherwise changing DoorLoop records is blocked.

blocked.label: Operate payments, accounting, leasing, or screening
blocked.description: Rent collection, outgoing payments, payment portals, owner distributions, accounting, financial reports, bank-linked data, applications, eSign, tenant screening, credit reporting, and legal-document workflows are blocked.

blocked.label: Run raw DoorLoop API requests
blocked.description: Arbitrary REST requests, OData query construction, unlisted endpoint discovery, browser-devtools endpoint mapping, custom payloads, and generic API proxying are blocked until Relay has a typed approved operation contract.

blocked.label: Use private DoorLoop access
blocked.description: Browser automation, session cookies, user passwords, private APIs, traffic inspection, screen scraping, unofficial endpoints, and provider-console activity are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No DoorLoop action is enabled until DoorLoop and Relay approve the integration, credentials, API terms, typed operations, user and portfolio binding, property-management data categories, payments/accounting/screening/leasing exclusions, limits, audit, retention, revocation, and disconnect behavior.

runtimeSupport.description: No DoorLoop tools are mounted until approved API access, terms, credentials, and bounded typed property-management operations are accepted.
No DoorLoop tools are mounted until approved API access, terms, credentials, and bounded typed property-management operations are accepted.

providerSetup.blocker: DoorLoop publishes REST API reference materials and support documentation stating that the API gives approved developers secure access to DoorLoop account data, uses resource-oriented URLs, JSON request and response bodies, standard HTTP responses, authentication, verbs, and OData queries. DoorLoop partner materials also say API access is selective to protect the software and prevent spam or unnecessary calls, and that approved partners receive API access and documentation. The public materials do not give Relay an approved credential, partner status, customer authorization, API Terms acceptance, credential scope, tenant and portfolio binding, safe operation allowlist, payments/accounting/screening/leasing exclusions, raw OData policy, rate-limit contract, revocation, audit, retention, or disconnect behavior.
providerSetup.nextAction: Product, partnerships, legal, privacy, security, property-management, payments/accounting, screening, leasing, communications, and provider-console owners must apply for or otherwise obtain approved DoorLoop API access and current API terms. Before implementation, freeze credential ownership, API-key issuance and revocation, exact endpoints, OData filters, readable fields, write authority, payments/accounting exclusions, tenant and owner consent, legal-document and screening constraints, resident communications rules, fair-housing and privacy controls, audit, retention, redaction, deletion, and disconnect behavior, then complete live acceptance in the provider-console task.

evidence.supports: DoorLoop's API reference says the DoorLoop API gives approved developers secure access to account data and is organized around REST with resource-oriented URLs, JSON bodies, HTTP response codes, authentication, and verbs.
DoorLoop's support article links to the API reference and tells developers where to find API documentation, while also discussing existing connections and API-request troubleshooting.

DoorLoop's partner page says the REST API offers two-way read and write access, supports OData queries, and that API access is selective; applicants are approved before receiving access and documentation.
DoorLoop's integrations page presents Zapier, partner integrations, and an open API/build-your-own path for connected property-management workflows.
DoorLoop's FAQ describes property-management use cases across tenant and lease tracking, rent and fee collection, accounting and reporting, maintenance, and API security.

DoorLoop publishes legal agreements including API Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, financial-services, outgoing-payment, owner-portal, payment-portal, tenant-portal, TransUnion, and other terms relevant to a property-management integration.
